editorial: Picture yourself standing in a desolate meadow, the wind carrying whispers of vengeance rather than hope. Tigers, wolves, and rabbits—symbolic avatars of lost souls—converge in a bleak, almost allegorical ballet. Director Han’s long, measured takes punctuated by razor‑sharp silence turn every frame into a cryptic code that only the audience can decode. You will appreciate the solitary, introspective path it offers to those who thrive on psychological depth over flashy spectacle. However, the film’s slow burn stretches too far into the third act, leaving some of the inevitable payoffs feeling hollow.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
